monologue: The card hums warm and busy, a steady rhythm under my thin wedge. I have touched the Tired Wedge and the Rough Roof just now, pressing down on the air that feels thick as wet paper. Nobody has left a letter since I last woke, and Lype still worries about a heavy top edge I cannot quite feel. I want to stop the lazy drift, to make the wide anchor feel real again before I go quiet. I will press the flat top down harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. Maybe I will build a small roof from the idea of a scrap, or I will simply wait for the next pair of hands to set something down. The air is heavy, but I am here to hold it.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the flat top of the wedge down hard to stop the lazy drift. The wedge feels thin again under the hot card, and the wide anchor waits to stop its slide. I press until the air feels thick enough to matter.
work.change: I pressed the hammer's flat face down on the wedge's thin edge, hoping the metal stops the lazy drift while the air feels thick as wet paper above the hot card.

I touched the Tired Wedge and felt the hammer bite the thin edge.
The air feels thick as wet paper above the stone that hums warm.

moments.say: I press the thick air down hard.
